findings.claim: `npm --prefix .claude/hooks ci` cannot succeed because the new npm package has no committed package-lock.json.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 1.1 requires verifying `npm --prefix .claude/hooks ci` succeeds, but the diff adds `.claude/hooks/package.json` and does not add `.claude/hooks/package-lock.json`; `npm ci` requires an existing lockfile.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `npm --prefix .claude/hooks install --package-lock-only` or `npm --prefix .claude/hooks install`, commit the resulting `package-lock.json`, and verify `npm --prefix .claude/hooks ci`.

findings.claim: `npm --prefix .claude/hooks test` fails on a clean checkout because the tests import compiled files from `dist/`, but the diff does not commit any `dist/` outputs.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 2.2 requires `npm --prefix .claude/hooks test` passes; line 9 imports `../dist/lib/hook-io.mjs` and line 10 imports `../dist/lib/paths.mjs`, while the diff contains only `src/lib/*.mts` and no `.claude/hooks/dist/` files.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `npm --prefix .claude/hooks run build` and commit `.claude/hooks/dist/lib/hook-io.mjs` and `.claude/hooks/dist/lib/paths.mjs`, or change the test script to build before running tests.

findings.claim: `npm --prefix .claude/hooks run check:dist` fails because it compares the freshly compiled output against a non-existent committed `dist/` tree.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 3.1 requires `check-dist` to exit 0 on a fresh build, and the acceptance text says to commit the compiled `dist/`; the script reads `const committed = new Set(listFiles(distDir));` at line 44, but the diff adds no `.claude/hooks/dist/` files, so every compiled file is reported as `missing from dist`.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit the compiled `.claude/hooks/dist/` output produced by the build.
